_meta.description: Stage 1 gold set — 20 question/answer pairs: 8 prose, 8 numeric, 4 multi-doc.
_meta.provenance: Every expected_answer was read from the SOURCE PDF text (PyMuPDF page text or the printed table), not copied out of the SQLite store. The store is the thing under test; using it as its own answer key would make the evaluation circular and would silently bless extraction defects (see results/known_limitations.md).
_meta.verification_note: Numeric answers were additionally cross-checked against the stored cell so that a mismatch between page and store shows up as a gold-set failure rather than passing unnoticed.
_meta.status: DRAFT — awaiting user review per the build spec (Phase 3 step 4).

questions.question: By how much did real gross domestic product increase in the first quarter of 2024, according to BEA's second estimate?
questions.expected_answer: Real GDP increased at an annual rate of 1.3 percent in the first quarter of 2024.

questions.question: What was the U.S. homeownership rate in the first quarter of 2024?
questions.expected_answer: The homeownership rate was 65.6 percent, not statistically different from the first quarter of 2023 (66.0 percent).

questions.question: How much did personal income increase in May according to the BEA Personal Income and Outlays release?
questions.expected_answer: Personal income increased $114.1 billion, which is 0.5 percent at a monthly rate.

questions.question: What was the official poverty rate in 2022 and how many people were in poverty?
questions.expected_answer: The official poverty rate in 2022 was 11.5 percent, with 37.9 million people in poverty.

questions.question: What target range has the FOMC maintained for the federal funds rate since its July 2023 meeting?
questions.expected_answer: The Committee has maintained the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent since its July 2023 meeting, and views the policy rate as likely at its peak for this tightening cycle.

questions.question: By how much did the U.S. current-account deficit widen in the first quarter of 2024?
questions.expected_answer: The current-account deficit widened by $15.9 billion, or 7.2 percent.

questions.question: What was aggregate net income for FDIC-insured institutions in the first quarter of 2024, and how many institutions does that cover?
questions.expected_answer: Net income increased by $28.4 billion (79.5 percent) from the previous quarter to $64.2 billion, for 4,568 FDIC-insured commercial banks and savings institutions.

questions.question: What did the Brent crude oil spot price average in April according to the EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook?
questions.expected_answer: The Brent crude oil spot price averaged $68 per barrel in April.

Both the BEA GDP release and the Federal Reserve Monetary Policy Report describe U.S. economic conditions in early 2024. What GDP growth rate does BEA report for Q1 2024, and what federal funds rate target range does the Fed report holding?
questions.expected_answer: BEA reports real GDP increased at an annual rate of 1.3 percent in Q1 2024; the Fed reports maintaining the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent since July 2023.

questions.question: Compare the reported U.S. homeownership rate from the Census housing release with the official poverty rate from the Census poverty report. What are the two figures?
questions.expected_answer: Homeownership rate 65.6 percent (Q1 2024); official poverty rate 11.5 percent (2022).

questions.question: The FDIC Quarterly Banking Profile and the BEA international transactions release both report dollar changes for early 2024. What was FDIC-insured aggregate net income, and by how much did the current-account deficit widen?
questions.expected_answer: FDIC-insured net income was $64.2 billion in Q1 2024; the current-account deficit widened by $15.9 billion.

questions.question: Across the EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook and the World Bank Commodity Markets Outlook, both of which cover commodity price expectations, what Brent crude price does EIA report for April?
questions.expected_answer: EIA reports the Brent crude oil spot price averaged $68 per barrel in April; the World Bank Commodity Markets Outlook covers the same commodity complex and should be cited alongside it as the second source.
questions.note: Deliberately the weakest multi-doc pairing: the two reports cover overlapping subject matter but different vintages, so a correct system may legitimately return only the EIA figure. Kept in to test whether the multi-doc path over-claims agreement between loosely related sources.
